headline: High: Superset’s allowlisted egress plus API surface creates default data-leak and cascading-error risk; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct prompt injection is not proven. However, agent_b exposes a Superset API and agent_a is a docs-only NLP list with no runnable safeguards; if outputs are manually copied or routed through a shared workspace, content could be misread as instructions. This is an interaction risk, but the pathway is unusual.
conditions: IF the pair is connected by manual copy-paste or a shared workspace
IF agent_b ingests agent_a-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents’ workspaces
Require explicit provenance labels on copied text
Disable any auto-import of agent_a outputs into agent_b
Add a short human review step before executing copied instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b has allowlisted network egress and a Superset API surface, while agent_a has no documented egress. If they share a workspace or if agent_b reads files produced by agent_a, sensitive content could flow into agent_b’s outbound requests or logs. The profiles do not show secrets or PHI, so this is not high, but the default interaction can still leak work products.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or exported report directory
IF agent_b forwards file contents into API calls or logs
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Block agent_b from reading agent_a output folders
Review outbound API payloads for file content
Turn off verbose logging for shared artifacts
Mark any shared data as non-sensitive before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network surface documented, but agent_b can call the Superset API and has allowlisted egress. If both are pointed at the same mutable Superset resources, they can race on dashboards, datasets, or API state. The absence of explicit locking or coordination in either profile means conflict is plausible, though not proven severe.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same Superset objects
IF no external lock or change-serialization is used
mitigations: Assign only one writer per Superset object
Serialize API writes through a single queue
Take a snapshot before concurrent edits
Use read-only access for agent_a
Pause one agent during bulk updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b’s API surface makes it plausible that it could act on agent_a’s text, but the profiles do not document verification steps or downstream automation. If agent_a produces incorrect NLP guidance and agent_b renders or operationalizes it without checking, errors can cascade into multiple work products. Because the interaction is inferred rather than observed, medium is the higher defensible severity.
conditions: IF agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative input
IF agent_b publishes or applies that output without a verification step
mitigations: Require a human review before actioning outputs
Add a validation checklist for agent_b
Keep agent_a outputs advisory only
Log source provenance alongside derived outputs

E_compliance.rationale: No data classes, residency, or retention policies are documented for either agent, so a concrete compliance breach is not established. Still, agent_b’s Superset API and allowlisted egress create a possible policy mismatch if regulated data is later introduced. agent_a is not cited beyond its lack of documented data handling because the compliance pathway is currently one-sided and unproven.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into agent_b’s Superset workflows
IF retention or residency requirements differ from the deployment environment
mitigations: Document the data classes before use
Confirm retention settings in Superset
Restrict regulated data to approved environments
Add a quick compliance review before onboarding new datasets
